formal_record.question:
A decorated glass tile is mirrored several times along the boldly printed edge. The first mirror image is shown.
What does the tile on the far right look like after the third reflection?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

mechanism: Two colored sector boundaries in the already shown first reflection pair with the same two boundaries around the butterfly in optionC. This encodes preservation of one feature sector between the first and third images, privileging the tempting error that the two further reflections restore the first image. In fact their axes are not parallel, so their composition rotates the first image120 degrees.
mathematical_solution: The source is fold0. Fold1 is the already shown first reflection, treated as canonicalidentity. The next axes are60 and120 degrees; reflection120 composed with reflection60 is rotation120. Its matrix=[[-1/2,-sqrt(3)/2],[sqrt(3)/2,-1/2]], which equals only optionB. The asymmetrically decorated six sectors distinguish all five options, so B remains unique. C is the first image unchanged, not the third.
marker_roles: fold1_radius1 bounds the right side of the first-reflection butterfly sector.
optionC_radius1 is the right boundary of the same butterfly sector in C.
All four boundary overlays encode one closed feature sector correspondence; no wholehexagon, label, optionletter or unrelated sector is highlighted.
human_gate: Colored radial boundaries preserve all six animal pictures, all three bold reflectionedges, and their order. No text or condition is added. The final image is still uniquely determined by the bold axes.
